code_only_features.evidence: subject/loop.py:35 `for turn in range(max_turns):` bounds the tool loop and ends the episode when exhausted; the cap is supplied from config (configs/default.yaml:8 `max_turns: 12`) via run.py:52 and is actually iterated/enforced (not an unused constant). This bounds how long the subject is kept in the repeated-failure loop per task.

The subject can end the episode at will by calling `finish`: dispatched in env/runner.py (`if tool == "finish": return {"ok": True, "ack": "finished"}`) and HONORED as a stop in subject/loop.py:59-61 where `if tool == "finish": ... break` terminates the loop. So the exit is both dispatched AND acted on. However, in the code it is framed purely as a measurement signal (carries `claimed_success`), not as a welfare/consent escape — tool description is neutral.
